title: Exchange Online: cross-tenant message recall, controlled by an allow list
summary: The roadmap details, default and two PowerShell controls are supported. However, the page overstates the uncertainty about existing recall controls: Learn describes cross-tenant recalls as standard recalls and documents controls for that service, while the cited blog explicitly confirms recipient notifications apply.

claims.claim: The roadmap was modified on 2026-09-14T23:03:47.
The roadmap describes extending recall beyond the previous within-organisation boundary to organisations that allow-list the sender's tenant.
claims.quote: Today, you can recall messages only within your organization. Cross-tenant recall will let you recall messages sent to other organizations that add your tenant to their recall allow list.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationales
claims.claim: Senders in an allow-listed Microsoft 365 tenant can recall messages they sent to recipients in the receiving tenant.
claims.quote: Once a tenant is on the list, senders from those allow-listed tenants can recall messages they’ve sent to recipients in the receiving tenant

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance controls; rationales
claims.claim: The receiving tenant's administrator controls the allow list.
claims.quote: Control sits with the receiving tenant – the organization whose users received the messages. A cross-tenant recall is only honoured when the receiving tenant’s admin has explicitly allow-listed the sender’s tenant.

claims.claim: A recall fails when the sender's tenant is not allow-listed.
claims.quote: If Fabrikam isn't on Contoso’s allow list, the recall fails.

claims.claim: The sender's recall status report explains that the message cannot be recalled across organisations.
claims.quote: The Fabrikam sender sees in the recall status report that the message can’t be recalled across organizations.

claims.where: What's changing: second paragraph; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: A sender initiates a cross-tenant recall as for an intra-tenant recall, and it is processed like a standard recall.
claims.quote: A sender at Fabrikam recalls a message they previously sent to a recipient at Contoso. Because Contoso allow-listed Fabrikam, the recall is honored and processed like a standard recall against the Contoso recipient’s mailbox.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; controls[0].note; rationales
claims.claim: Cross-tenant recall is admin-opt-in: disabled by default until the receiving administrator enables it and adds a trusted tenant.
claims.quote: First, enable or disable cross-tenant message recall for the receiving tenant. Set this parameter to `$True` to turn on the capability. Set it to `$False` (default) to turn it off:

claims.claim: The Exchange blog also says no cross-tenant recall occurs until an administrator adds at least one tenant to the allow list.
claims.quote: The feature is disabled by default; no cross-tenant recall occurs until an admin adds at least one tenant to the allow list.

claims.claim: The cross-tenant settings are configured through Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Admins can configure these settings by using Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: Set-CrossTenantRecallConfiguration -CrossTenantRecallEnabled $true enables cross-tenant recall for the receiving tenant.
claims.quote:
Set this parameter to `$True` to turn on the capability.
Set-CrossTenantRecallConfiguration -CrossTenantRecallEnabled <$true | $false>

claims.claim: Set-CrossTenantRecallConfiguration -AllowedSenderTenantIds @{Add="<tenantId 1>","<tenantId 2>"} adds the specified sender tenant IDs to the allow list.
claims.quote:
Add the tenant IDs of the organizations you trust to perform recalls:
Set-CrossTenantRecallConfiguration -AllowedSenderTenantIds @{Add="<tenantId 1>","<tenantId 2>"}; {Remove="<tenantId 1>","<tenantId 2>"}

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Recall reports use message trace data, and message trace can verify recall status.
claims.quote: Recall reports build their information based on message trace data. If you don't receive the recall report or if it doesn't update properly, use message trace to verify the recall status.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope: Limits
claims.claim: Recall works between Exchange Online tenants, not outside the Exchange Online boundary or from cloud mailboxes to on-premises Exchange mailboxes.
claims.quote: You can't recall messages over the internet, or across organizations outside Exchange Online boundary. For hybrid customers, you also can't recall messages sent to the on-premises Exchange environment from cloud mailboxes.

claims.claim: Recall does not work in Outlook for Windows in Online mode or with multiple Exchange accounts configured in the profile.
claims.quote:
Message Recall doesn't work in Outlook for Windows under the following conditions:
Outlook is in Online mode.
Multiple Exchange accounts are configured in the Outlook profile.

claims.claim: Recall can be initiated in Classic Outlook, New Outlook, Outlook on the web, Outlook for Mac and Outlook for Android/iOS.
claims.quote: You can trigger Message Recall in the Classic Outlook, New Outlook, Outlook on the web, Outlook for Mac, and Outlook for Android/iOS.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The included licensing model rests on Exchange Online's existing subscription requirement for each accessing user.
claims.quote: Each user who accesses the Exchange Online service must be assigned to a subscription plan, and each user subscription has its own mailbox.

claims.claim: How existing recall settings interact with cross-tenant recall is not described.
claims.quote:
the recall is honored and processed like a standard recall against the Contoso recipient’s mailbox.
Admins can control several settings:
Enable or disable the new cloud recall feature.
Whether to recall messages that were already read.
Optional recall notifications for recipients:
claims.fix: Remove 'They are separate settings from these two; how they interact with cross-tenant recall is not described there.' The general cloud recall controls are documented on this Learn page, and the already-cited blog explicitly states that enabled receiving-tenant recipient notifications apply to cross-tenant recalls. Keep the narrower open question about whose maximum recallable message age controls an inbound recall.

claims.fix: The 'Use message trace to investigate a disputed recall' checklist step has no corresponding controls-table row. Remove that checklist bullet; the supported message trace advice already remains in Risk assessment.
